articles.title_original: At least 33 pupils and teacher killed after school roof collapses in Pakistan
articles.title_zh: At least 33 pupils and teacher killed after school roof collapses in Pakistan
facts_zh:
At least 33 pupils and teacher killed after school roof collapses in Pakistan
- Published
At least 33 pupils and a teacher have been killed after a school roof collapsed in the north-western Pakistani city of Peshawar, according to hospital officials.
More than a dozen others are injured, with some in a critical condition.
Emergency services were called to the private Al-Khair school in Dir Colony at 08:48 (03:48 GMT) on Thursday after lessons had begun, rescue official Bilal Faizi told the BBC.

all_titles.en: At least 33 pupils and teacher killed after school roof collapses in Pakistan

articles.title_original: Trump calls off livestream for Fort Hood shooter's execution by firing squad
articles.title_zh: Trump calls off livestream for Fort Hood shooter's execution by firing squad
facts_zh:
Trump calls off livestream for Fort Hood shooter's execution by firing squad
- Published
US President Donald Trump has called off plans to livestream the execution of former US army psychiatrist Nidal Hasan by firing squad.
Trump had previously said he approved of showing online the death of the Fort Hood attacker, while Vice-President JD Vance cast doubt on whether it would happen and said he would not watch it.
As criticism over the public display mounted, Trump said on Thursday that "many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die".

all_titles.en: Trump calls off livestream for Fort Hood shooter's execution by firing squad

articles.title_original: Tech market sell-off deepens amid fears over US inflation and AI debt
articles.title_zh: Tech market sell-off deepens amid fears over US inflation and AI debt
facts_zh: Chip makers and tech investors such as Samsung and SoftBank plunge as potential interest rate hikes spook markets Business news – live updates Larry Elliott: the global economy is muddling through.

But a storm is coming An accelerating sell-off of AI-linked shares has hit global markets, as fears over rising inflation and future interest rate hikes spooked traders already wary of the heavily indebted sector.

South Korea’s benchmark Kospi 200 index, which is heavily skewed towards the companies that make memory chips, fell more than 8% overnight to a six-month closing low, triggering circuit breakers that brought trading to a halt at various points.

articles.title_original: Obama says drift towards extremism 'not inevitable'
articles.title_zh: Obama says drift towards extremism 'not inevitable'
facts_zh:
Obama says drift towards extremism 'not inevitable'
- Published
Barack Obama has told an audience in Glasgow that hope is worth fighting for despite big challenges facing the modern world.
The 44th president of the United States said online platforms had shifted in recent years to focus on content that stoked anger and fear, but he believes a drift to extremism is "not inevitable".
The comments came as he addressed an OVO Hydro crowd of 12,150 people while in conversation with British journalist and author Sathnam Sanghera, part of three speaking dates in the UK.

all_titles.en: Obama says drift towards extremism 'not inevitable'

articles.title_original: Two dead in Istanbul after heaviest rainfall in 84 years, governor says
articles.title_zh: Two dead in Istanbul after heaviest rainfall in 84 years, governor says
facts_zh:
Two dead in Istanbul after heaviest rainfall in 84 years, governor says
- Published
Two people have died after severe flooding caused by what the governor of Istanbul said was the heaviest rainfall in 84 years, BBC Turkish has reported.
A14-year-old boy died after he was electrocuted when he stepped in a puddle, while a 34-year-old man attempting to cross the road slipped and fell, hitting his head on the pavement.
Nearly 600 people have been rescued after becoming stranded, the city's deputy mayor said, with cars submerged in water in some districts.

all_titles.en: Two dead in Istanbul after heaviest rainfall in 84 years, governor says

articles.title_original: Brazil's Congress approves shorter working week in win for Lula
articles.title_zh: Brazil's Congress approves shorter working week in win for Lula
facts_zh:
Brazil's Congress approves shorter working week in win for Lula
- Published
Brazil's Congress has approved a constitutional amendment that will cut the working week from 44 hours to 40 and give employees two days off per week without cutting their salary.
The change represents the biggest overhaul to workers' rights since Brazil's return to democracy in 1988.
Senators passed the amendment, which left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva had championed, less than two weeks before a second round in the Latin American nation's presidential election.

all_titles.en: Brazil's Congress approves shorter working week in win for Lula

articles.title_zh: Actor Imran Khan ordered to leave India after participating in protest
facts_zh:
Actor Imran Khan ordered to leave India after participating in protest
- Published
Authorities in India have ordered actor Imran Khan, nephew of Bollywood star Aamir Khan, to leave the country by 28 October after he participated in a protest, seeking electoral reforms.
An American citizen, Khan holds an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, which allows people of Indian origin to visit and stay in the country.
But an OCI cannot vote or contest elections.

articles.title_zh: Australian woman charged with lacing colleague's curry with snail poison
facts_zh:
Australian woman charged with lacing colleague's curry with snail poison
- Published
An Australian woman has been charged after allegedly lacing a colleague's curry with snail poison.
Police in the state of Western Australia say the alleged victim made a meal for her co-workers in February, which they shared at morning tea.
But when the 58-year-old returned to eat leftovers at lunch, she noticed bright green granules in the food and that her tongue felt numb after tasting it.

articles.title_zh: Australia's first-ever Michelin stars go to 11 restaurants in one state
facts_zh:
Australia's first-ever Michelin stars go to 11 restaurants in one state
- Published
Australia has been awarded its first Michelin stars, with 11 restaurants in the state of South Australia receiving the distinction.
Magill Estate Restaurant in Adelaide was the only venue to receive two stars, while 10 others were awarded one star each.
South Australia's government paid for incognito inspectors to visit the state, according to national broadcaster ABC, which is why no spots have been recognised in other parts of the country.

articles.title_original: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds
articles.title_zh: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds
facts_zh:
Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds
- Published
Elon Musk has suggested that the US government may be behind restrictions on the speed at which some of Ukraine's weapons can travel and stay connected to SpaceX's Starlink internet network.

Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to guide drones to Russian targets and also protect its own skies, but on Tuesday night Ukraine said unexpected new speed limits were disrupting its battlefield missions.
An adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky said he believed the restrictions were not a coincidence and were related to the latest strains between Kyiv and Washington.

all_titles.en: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds

articles.title_original: Student protesters attack government buildings in Albania
articles.title_zh: Student protesters attack government buildings in Albania
facts_zh:
Student protesters attack government buildings in Albania
- Published
Thousands of students have taken to the streets in the Albanian capital of Tirana, attacking several government buildings on the second day of violent anti-government protests.
The demonstration began outside the ministry of education on Tuesday, as students called for better university conditions and job prospects.
Wednesday saw part of the education ministry's building set on fire, while the prime minister's office, finance and interior ministry, and several surrounding businesses were also attacked.

all_titles.en: Student protesters attack government buildings in Albania

articles.title_zh: Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza denies using AI to write prize-winning story
facts_zh: Article in Atlantic claims The Blue Fighter was artificially generated, days after it won Caine prize for African writers The Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied using AI to write a prize-winning short story after an article in the Atlantic said software had flagged it as almost completely AI-generated.
Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter was announced as the winner of the prestigious Caine prize for African writers on 6 October.
Five days later, The Atlantic published an article by the author and journalist Vauhini Vara titled: “Yet Another Literary prize winner Seems to Be AI.” Continue reading...

articles.title_zh: Burnham says he wants to 'repair bridges' between Ukraine and US
facts_zh:
Burnham says he wants to 'repair bridges' between Ukraine and US
- Published
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he will try to "repair bridges" between Ukraine and the United States, ahead of a meeting with President Volodymyr Zelensky at Downing Street.
The Ukrainian president was welcomed by a military ceremonial guard outside Number 10 as he arrived for the meeting, in what is thought to be a first for a foreign leader.
It comes after President Donald Trump said he had struck a deal with Moscow to import Russian diesel.

all_titles.en: Burnham says he wants to 'repair bridges' between Ukraine and US

articles.title_original: Pope walking and recovering 'as expected' after surgery, doctors say
articles.title_zh: Pope walking and recovering 'as expected' after surgery, doctors say
facts_zh:
Pope walking and recovering 'as expected' after surgery, doctors say
- Published
Pope Leo XIV's recovery from surgery to remove a lower lobe of his lung is "progressing as expected", his doctors have said.
The 71-year-old pontiff has started to walk and has "resumed a normal diet" following the roughly 90-minute procedure, the medics said in an update shared by the Vatican.
The Pope was diagnosed with lung cancer after the surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, which the Vatican said had been "successful" and proceeded without complications.

all_titles.en: Pope walking and recovering 'as expected' after surgery, doctors say

articles.title_zh: Hundreds of thousands of workers on strike across Republic of Ireland
facts_zh:
Hundreds of thousands of workers on strike across Republic of Ireland
- Published
More than 300,000 workers, including nurses, doctors, teachers and civil servants, are on strike across the Republic of Ireland.
It comes amid an ongoing pay dispute between public sector workers and the Irish government, with a further strike planned on 21 October.
It is expected schools could be closed with hospital appointments cancelled and picket lines formed across the country during the 24-hour strike.

articles.title_original: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
articles.title_zh: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
facts_zh:
Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
- Published
A Ukrainian man has gone on trial in Hamburg accused of blowing up Russia's Nord Stream gas pipelines to Germany, four years after one of the most dramatic acts of sabotage in modern European history.
Prosecutors say Serhii Kuznetsov played a leading role in a team of saboteurs that destroyed the pipelines, accusing him of a war crime.
His defence has called for the case to be dismissed.

all_titles.en: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
